perspective:
From Gloria Bangura’s perspective:

- I work with Donald at a large event planning company. I’m an administrative assistant, and he bartends during company events. We’re colleagues but not personally close; we mainly interact at these events.
- Over several events, I noticed Donald seemed distracted and less enthusiastic while serving drinks. I started to think he might be unhappy with his job.
- I approached him and asked if he was okay with the job. He told me he wasn’t as into it as he used to be and that it felt repetitive.
- After that conversation, I thought more about it and suspected his work dissatisfaction might be connected to larger personal issues.
- I suggested he consider talking to a professional. He said he hadn’t really considered it and wasn’t sure it would help.
- After that, I sensed a shift in his behavior toward me and worried he might resent my suggestion as an overstep.
- I apologized, saying I only wanted to help and didn’t mean to make assumptions. He told me he was a bit taken aback at first but knew I meant well and said it was a lot to process.
- I felt relieved that the tension eased. I invited him to collaborate on a new project, saying it could use his creative input. He agreed and said it sounded like a great opportunity.
- After the project, I saw how much he contributed and noticed renewed enthusiasm from him. I believed he was a valuable team member.
- I publicly acknowledged his work in a meeting and said his efforts were crucial to the project’s success. He thanked me and said it meant a lot to him and that he felt great to be appreciated.
final_response:
I wanted to help because I noticed Donald seemed unhappy, so I initiated a conversation with him about how he was feeling.

ANSWER: C
